findings.obligation: P7: the pure edge rule names exactly the sides with hidden columns within one pixel. Testing Theater, circular verification (BLOCKER).
findings.observation: BLOCKING. Line 40 reads: if (contentWidth <= viewportWidth + 1) return "none"; Production horizontalOverflow.ts:15 reads: if (contentWidth <= viewportWidth + TOLERANCE_PX) return "none";. expectedEdges (lines 41-46) repeats the production formula and branch order, so the property compares production with a copy of itself. The only literal expectation for the rule is the single case at lines 91-94 (overflowEdges(500, 1000, 900) gives none). The boundary examples at lines 75-83 also feed through expectedEdges and assert no literal sides.
findings.remediation: Replace expectedEdges with literal rows of (scrollLeft, viewportWidth, contentWidth) to sides, written from the rule in words, covering the one-pixel boundary, the fit case and the stale-scroll case. Keep the fast-check property only for invariants that do not restate the formula, for example: none whenever contentWidth is at most viewportWidth plus 1; left is named only when scrollLeft exceeds 1.

findings.obligation: P8 Expected: the actions cell takes the focus and lies inside the visible range. Testing Theater, mock returns the expected value (BLOCKER).
findings.observation: BLOCKING. The stub at line 231 returns { left: PINNED_LEFT, right: 400 } for the actions cell, a fixed value that production never changes. Assertions at lines 309-311 (left >= 0) and 313-315 (right <= VIEW_RIGHT) hold for the authored stub whatever DataGridBase does, so removing scrollFocusedCellIntoView still passes them. Only the focus check in whenTheyArrowToTheCell is real.
findings.remediation: Delete the two actions geometry assertions. Keep the focus assertion. Move the claim that the actions cell is inside the visible table to the Playwright spec, where the browser measures it, or derive the pinned place from the scroll model the test drives.

findings.obligation: P6/P7 Expected: the right overlay shows only when right or both, the left only when left or both.
findings.observation: NON-BLOCKING. Line 187 checks only the count of decorative overlays (toHaveLength), not their side. Swapping the left and right overlays in DataGridBase.tsx OverflowCue (lines 314-319) keeps this test green. The Playwright spec catches the swap at 1280 px (spec line 74), at 375 px (line 102) and at end of range (line 109), so this gap is covered at E2E only.
findings.remediation: Assert the side of each overlay in jsdom, for example through a data-side attribute or the computed left or right, so the Expected clause is checked where it is cheap.

findings.remediation: Add a 375 px case with the Name width stored at 900 px, or record the fitted-layout choice as the deliberate stimulus in acceptance.md P11.

findings.obligation: E2E learnings: a page object must not map not found to a real value.
findings.observation: NON-BLOCKING. sidesWithACue returns an empty array when the [data-overflow] root or its cues are missing. [] is a real value, so the spec check at lines 58-60 (no shadow on a table that fits) passes if the root selector stops matching.
findings.remediation: Assert the [data-overflow] table root exists once (for example toHaveCount(1)) before reading its cues, so a missing root fails instead of reading as no shadow.

findings.obligation: E2E learnings: wait for the settled state, not a snapshot.
findings.observation: NON-BLOCKING. Line 102 expect(await reports.sidesWithACue()).toEqual(["right"]) is a one-shot read right after the viewport change; the cue comes from the grid measurement, which the name-width poll does not wait for. Line 74 has the same pattern after reopen. Lines 104-109 already poll the end-of-range state.
findings.remediation: Read the sides inside expect.poll with a message at lines 74 and 102, as lines 104-109 do.

findings.obligation: Test-writing: a test must not depend on machinery the GREEN state no longer needs; the module graph must show the dependency.
findings.observation: NON-BLOCKING. Lines 21-22 import a variable specifier with a vite-ignore comment, and lines 13-17 map load errors to an empty object. The module now exists, so this RED scaffolding is dead. A variable specifier is invisible to tsc and to the vitest module graph, so a change to horizontalOverflow.ts does not select this file under --changed.
findings.remediation: Use a static import: import { overflowEdges } from "./horizontalOverflow"; and delete MODULE, isModuleNotFound and loadOverflowEdges.
